newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba toughens penal code to deal with prostitution.
newsitem.headline: Cuba toughens penal code to deal with prostitution.

text.p: Cuba has toughened its penal code to deal with offences involving prostitution, pimping and corruption of minors, Justice Minister Roberto Diaz said on Tuesday.

The Cuban news agency Prensa Latina quoted Diaz as saying the changes to the penal code were contained in a decree law that was published this week in the official gazette and will come into force in two months.
Diaz said the penal code had been widened to establish punishment for pimping and profiting from prostitution.

The basic penalty for this will be a jail term of two to five years. There are provisions for three-to-eight-year jail terms if the person involved works in public health, law and order, education or tourism.

Penalties for corruption of minors, or the use of children for sexual practices, prostitution or pornographic acts, range between eight and 20 years, Prensa Latina said. To date, the jail term for introducing a minor to prostitution was five years.
"We have as a principle that we want to develop tourism that is exempt from prostitution, gambling or drugs," Diaz said.

Prostitution, banned in Cuba after President Fidel Castro's 1959 revolution, has re-emerged in the past five years amid economic crisis and the increase in foreign tourists and businessmen visiting the island.

Authorities have acknowledged the problem, and have said they want to discourage the idea of Cuba as a sex destination. Since late 1995 there have been measures at many tourist hotels to prevent them being used by prostitutes, and periodic round-ups of people suspected of being prostitutes.
